title: BNCI 2014-008 P300 dataset (ALS patients)
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 8 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) performing a P300-based brain-computer interface (BCI) speller task. Participants completed a copy-spelling paradigm using a 6×6 matrix with row-column intensification, generating 35 trials per subject across a single session. The preprocessed data, acquired at 256 Hz from 8 scalp electrodes, demonstrates high classification accuracy (97.5%) and represents a clinically relevant application of P300-based communication systems for severely paralyzed individuals.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 8 ALS patients using 8 active electrodes (Fz, Cz, Pz, Oz, P3, P4, PO7, PO8) in a 10-10 montage with g.MOBILAB hardware and BCI2000 software. Sampling rate was 256 Hz with online bandpass filtering (0.1-10 Hz) and 50 Hz notch filtering. Reference electrode was placed at the right earlobe with ground at left mastoid. Preprocessing included offline bandpass filtering (0.1-10 Hz, 4th-order Butterworth), notch filtering at 50 Hz, artifact rejection (amplitude threshold ±70 μV), and baseline correction using 200 ms pre-stimulus intervals. Participants performed a copy-spelling task with 7 words of 5 characters each using visual feedback in a synchronous, online mode.
